title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with critical exceptional points governing their emergence.
motivation: Continuous time-translation symmetry breaking in open quantum systems is a key phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, but the conditions for its appearance are not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze a Lindblad master equation and map the steady state to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, identifying exceptional points that signal the transition to time-crystal behavior.
result: They demonstrate that the time-crystal phase corresponds to a PT-symmetric state, and the critical exceptional points mark the boundaries of the time-crystal regime.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for understanding continuous time crystals in open quantum systems, linking them to PT symmetry and exceptional points, which has implications for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium phases.

title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility In Optical Bistability
authors: G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, And S. R. K. Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): G. Keijsers, R. M. de Boer, B. Verdonschot, K. J. H. Peters, and S. R. K. Rodriguez

We demonstrate thermodynamic irreversibility in the stochastic switching of a coherently driven bistable optical cavity. We present measurements of phase space probability currents evidencing the breaking of detailed balance associated with thermodynamic irreversibility. We also estimate the magnitu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253803] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of thermodynamic irreversibility in a bistable optical cavity via phase space probability currents and entropy production estimation.
motivation: To directly observe and quantify thermodynamic irreversibility in a driven optical system, bridging stochastic thermodynamics and quantum optics.
method: Measurements of phase space probability currents in a coherently driven bistable optical cavity, combined with estimation of entropy production rate.
result: Clear evidence of broken detailed balance and nonzero entropy production, demonstrating irreversibility in the stochastic switching dynamics.
conclusion: Optical bistability provides a clean platform for studying thermodynamic irreversibility, with implications for understanding dissipation in driven quantum systems.

title: Shake Before Use: Universal Enhancement Of Quantum Thermometry By Unitary Driving
authors: Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, And Giacomo Guarnieri
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Tumbiolo, Lorenzo Maccone, Chiara Macchiavello, Matteo G. A. Paris, and Giacomo Guarnieri

Quantum thermometry aims at determining temperature with ultimate precision in the quantum regime. Standard equilibrium approaches, limited by the quantum Fisher information given by static energy fluctuations, lose sensitivity outside a fixed temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies have there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250401] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that applying a unitary driving pulse universally enhances the precision of quantum thermometry beyond the standard equilibrium limit.
motivation: Equilibrium quantum thermometry is limited by static energy fluctuations and loses sensitivity outside a narrow temperature window. Nonequilibrium strategies are needed to overcome these limitations.
method: The authors propose a protocol where a unitary driving pulse is applied to the probe before measurement, and they analyze the resulting quantum Fisher information to quantify the enhancement in temperature estimation precision.
result: They prove that for any finite-dimensional probe, there exists a unitary driving that increases the quantum Fisher information beyond the equilibrium value, and they demonstrate this enhancement for specific systems.
conclusion: Unitary driving provides a universal and practical method to improve quantum thermometry, with potential applications in nanoscale temperature sensing.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies for interacting scalar fields can be computed via free energy of replicas with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation from correlation functions.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but computing it for interacting quantum field theories is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method using correlation functions.
method: They derive a replica trick where odd-order Rényi entropies are expressed as free energy differences of a replicated system with additional quadratic couplings within the subsystem. This allows computation via two-point correlation functions using Wick's theorem.
result: The method is demonstrated for free fields and interacting fields in and out of equilibrium, showing that entanglement entropy can be extracted from correlation functions without needing full state tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for calculating entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, bridging quantum information and many-body physics, and is directly relevant to entanglement theory.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium thermometry using the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing how energy-level degeneracy and spectrum uniformity affect temperature sensitivity via quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Accurate temperature measurement at the quantum scale is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding how probe structure influences thermometric precision is key.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information for probes described by the multilevel quantum Rabi model, exploring the effects of degeneracy and spectrum uniformity on sensitivity.
result: Probes with degenerate energy levels can achieve higher peak sensitivity, while probes with more uniform spectra maintain sensitivity over a broader temperature range.
conclusion: The multilevel quantum Rabi model provides a versatile platform for quantum thermometry, with tunable sensitivity characteristics depending on the probe's spectral properties.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamics of nanoscale heat engines requires analyzing quantum working fluids, where fluctuations and quantum effects are significant.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator coupled to thermal baths.
result: They derive exact expressions for the cumulants of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and quantum signatures in the thermodynamic behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive thermodynamic analysis of a quantum resonator, highlighting the role of fluctuations and offering insights for quantum heat engine design.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for Petz f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) bound the precision of observables by entropy production, but existing TURs are limited to specific divergences. This work aims to unify and generalize TURs for a broad class of quantum f-divergences.
method: The author shows that any Petz f-divergence (with operator convex f) can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, using a mixture representation. This representation is then used to derive a TUR that holds for all such divergences.
result: A universal TUR is obtained: the distinguishability measured by any Petz f-divergence is bounded by the thermodynamic cost (e.g., entropy production) times a factor depending on f. This generalizes previous results for specific divergences like the relative entropy.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for thermodynamic uncertainty relations in quantum systems, highlighting the fundamental trade-off between distinguishability and thermodynamic cost, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols for detecting spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spins suffer from poor readout fidelity; dispersive measurements offer a non-destructive alternative with potential for quantum-limited sensitivity.
method: The authors theoretically model a cavity or resonator coupled to a spin ensemble, using input-output theory and quantum noise analysis to derive measurement imprecision and backaction.
result: They show that dispersive readout can achieve spin polarization sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, and identify optimal operating regimes for realistic experimental parameters.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-fidelity quantum noise detection in solid-state spin ensembles, enabling applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, showing that irreversibility at the ensemble level does not hold for individual quantum trajectories.
motivation: Open quantum systems typically exhibit irreversible dynamics when averaged over ensembles, but the behavior of individual trajectories under time reversal is less understood.
method: The authors analytically derive stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe reverse diffusion in quantum systems, using the formalism of quantum trajectories and time-reversal symmetry.
result: They demonstrate that reverse diffusion is possible at the trajectory level, with explicit equations governing the dynamics.
conclusion: The work reveals a fundamental asymmetry between ensemble and trajectory-level reversibility, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Optimal Work Extraction From Finite-time Closed Quantum Dynamics
authors: Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, And Ryusuke Hamazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shoki Sugimoto, Takahiro Sagawa, and Ryusuke Hamazaki

Extracting useful work from quantum systems is a fundamental problem in quantum thermodynamics. In scenarios where rapid protocols are desired—whether due to practical constraints or deliberate design choices—a fundamental trade-off between power and efficiency is yet to be established. Here, we inv…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on work extraction from finite-time closed quantum dynamics, revealing a trade-off between power and efficiency.
motivation: Understanding the limits of work extraction in quantum systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics, especially when rapid protocols are required.
method: The authors analyze finite-time closed quantum dynamics using optimal control theory and derive bounds on extractable work and power.
result: They establish a trade-off relation between power and efficiency, showing that faster protocols incur higher dissipation.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental constraints on quantum heat engines and inform the design of near-term quantum thermodynamic devices.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of Rains' quantum shadow enumerators in terms of Bell measurement statistics, enabling efficient experimental learning on a trapped-ion device.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for quantum error correction but lacked a direct physical interpretation, limiting their experimental accessibility.
method: The authors show that shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, and develop efficient learning protocols based on this connection, demonstrated on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: Experimental measurement of shadow enumerators is achieved, validating the theoretical interpretation and showing that these quantities can be efficiently estimated.
conclusion: This work bridges a gap between abstract error correction theory and experimental implementation, offering new tools for characterizing quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond and coupled individual tin-vacancy centers, measuring cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong spin-photon coupling suitable for quantum networking applications.
conclusion: This platform paves the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resources.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena within this unified rule.
result: The rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness and identifies intrinsically quantum properties in many processes long thought to be classical.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of quantumness and suggests that hidden quantum features could be harnessed for future technologies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a squeezed reservoir to create and stabilize multipartite entangled states, with reconfigurable coupling patterns.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate robust entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and simulate topological matter, with high fidelity and resilience to noise.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics using hybrid cavity-spin systems, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced discrete modulation (e.g., QPSK) with a new security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem to prove composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of over 1 Mbps over 50 km fiber, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: This work brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment, with potential for integration into quantum networks.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information survives in open or monitored systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurement outcomes are recorded, contrasting with the no-recording case where lifetime is constant. This reveals a new phase of information dynamics.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes provides a strategy to preserve fragile quantum information, improving the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, undermining quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in superconducting qubit platforms susceptible to ionizing radiation.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a superconducting qubit array with gap engineering, using radiation sources and measuring error correlations.
result: They discover that ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts that persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, posing a challenge for error correction.
conclusion: New mitigation strategies are needed to protect superconducting quantum processors from radiation-induced correlated errors to enable scalable quantum computing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global operations and optical heralding to generate entanglement.
result: They demonstrate sublinear experimental overhead for entanglement generation across 10–100 qubits, enabling large cluster states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scalable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of monitored quantum dynamics.
method: The authors analyze the decodability of quantum codes under random monitoring, using statistical mechanics mappings and insights from measurement-induced phase transitions.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and characterize the stability of encoded information under partial measurements.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, providing new perspectives on the interplay between measurements and quantum information protection.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a compact platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and complex. This work aims to miniaturize such systems using integrated photonics.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a Bell test to certify randomness, using integrated components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits with self-testing guarantees, achieving a randomness expansion rate suitable for practical applications while maintaining device independence.
conclusion: This demonstration shows that self-testing QRNGs can be realized on a scalable photonic platform, paving the way for compact, production-scale quantum security devices.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors develop a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of required emitters and increases the achievable distance for entanglement distribution under realistic loss.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree codes offer a practical path toward near-term quantum repeater implementations with improved performance.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional spin properties, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout; ZnO defects are underexplored compared to diamond or SiC.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of the electronic structure, spin coherence, and optical properties of the ZnO defect.
result: The defect exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive spin properties.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: The authors develop a composable security proof framework that incorporates device characterization parameters, allowing for practical security bounds.
result: The framework yields rigorous security guarantees that account for device imperfections, enabling standards and certification for QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and practice, providing a path to certified secure QKD with realistic devices.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all basic tasks in a single device is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the performance of superconducting qubit platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable quantum communication offers practical advantages over discrete-variable approaches, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and higher secret key rates in metropolitan distances.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne/heterodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental progress (CV-QKD, quantum repeaters, network demonstrations).
result: CV quantum communication is now a mature field with record-breaking key rates and field-tested systems, though challenges remain in long-distance transmission and integration with quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for practical quantum communication networks, with ongoing research addressing remaining hurdles.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical or conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing how entanglement generation can serve as a witness for quantum features of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for laboratory-based quantum gravity tests, bridging quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems with strong correlations, which are important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors extend many-body perturbation theory to open quantum systems by combining Keldysh and Lindblad formalisms, introducing diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism provides a systematic way to compute nonequilibrium steady states and response functions for driven dissipative quantum systems, capturing both coherent and dissipative dynamics.
conclusion: This work offers a powerful tool for analyzing quantum systems far from equilibrium, with applications to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information devices.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions and understand thermodynamic behavior of dynamical black holes.
method: Uses dynamical horizon framework and geometric analysis to derive a first law for non-equilibrium black holes.
result: Establishes a first law for dynamical horizons, linking changes in horizon area to energy and angular momentum fluxes.
conclusion: Black holes can be treated thermodynamically even when far from equilibrium, broadening the scope of black hole thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Nonreciprocity Through Squeezing-Induced Symmetry Breaking
authors: B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, And F. Nori
abstract:
Author(s): B.-B. Liu, D.-Y. Wang, J. Tang, G. Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, and F. Nori

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 253602] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities can exponentially enhance reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity, providing a new principle for unidirectional signal flow.
motivation: Nonreciprocal devices are essential for quantum information processing, but existing methods face limitations in isolation and bandwidth. The authors aim to develop a more efficient mechanism for enhancing nonreciprocity.
method: They establish a theoretical framework where squeezing in one cavity breaks the symmetry between two coupled cavities, leading to exponentially amplified nonreciprocity in the reservoir-mediated interaction. The model is analyzed using quantum master equations and input-output theory.
result: The squeezing-induced symmetry breaking yields an exponential enhancement of nonreciprocity, far beyond what simple coupling scaling can achieve, as demonstrated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a new guiding principle for engineering nonreciprocal devices, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Clifford Hierarchy Stabilizer Codes: Transversal Non-Clifford Gates And Magic States
authors: Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, And Po-Shen Hsin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryohei Kobayashi, Guanyu Zhu, and Po-Shen Hsin

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250802] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends topological stabilizer codes to Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes enabling transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound for topological stabilizer codes.
method: Generalizes Pauli stabilizer codes to Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes using higher-form symmetries and gauging, constructing codes with transversal non-Clifford gates.
result: Demonstrates that Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes can circumvent the Bravyi-König bound, allowing transversal T gates and magic state distillation.
conclusion: This work provides a new framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation with improved universality and dimensionality tradeoffs.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a noncommutative index for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, linking the transition to the noncommutativity of multi-site projection operators.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was unclear. The authors aim to provide an analytical understanding based on operator noncommutativity.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index defined via the algebraic structure of measurement operators and use it to characterize the entanglement phase transition in a class of measurement-only circuits.
result: The noncommutative index sharply distinguishes the volume-law and area-law phases, and its critical value matches numerical simulations. The transition is driven by the degree of noncommutativity among measurements.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a universal analytical tool for understanding entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, advancing the theory of quantum information dynamics.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a practical advantage.
method: The authors implement a higher-order power method on a quantum computer to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement.
result: The quantum algorithm is demonstrated on small systems, showing feasibility and potential speedup over classical methods.
conclusion: This work provides a proof-of-principle for quantum-assisted entanglement estimation, which could be useful for benchmarking quantum devices.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XXZ interactions and a staggered transverse field, showing that the dynamics effectively realize OAT in a collective spin subspace. They analyze the generation of entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing.
result: The proposed scheme generates scalable quantum resources, with entanglement and Bell correlations growing with system size, and spin squeezing reaching levels comparable to ideal OAT.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as scalable sources of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high efficiency.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes to avoid losses, limiting its speed. Accelerating the process violates adiabaticity, causing inefficiency.
method: The authors apply shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) via counter-diabatic driving to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic transitions.
result: The STA-based protocol achieves high-fidelity storage and retrieval in a fraction of the adiabatic time, with efficiency comparable to the adiabatic limit.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-performance quantum memories based on Rydberg EIT, benefiting quantum networks.

title: Entanglement Rényi Negativity Across The Finite-temperature Transition In The $o(3)$ Universality Class
authors: Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Xu Liu, Yi-Ming Ding, Zhe Wang, and Zheng Yan

The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions remains an open question, particularly for continuous symmetry breaking where zero-temperature Goldstone modes generate long-range correlations. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the third Rényi …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245145] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the third Rényi negativity across a finite-temperature phase transition in the O(3) universality class using quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions, especially with continuous symmetry breaking, is not well understood.
method: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the third Rényi negativity for the O(3) model.
result: The third Rényi negativity shows a peak near the critical temperature and obeys scaling laws consistent with the O(3) universality class.
conclusion: Entanglement measures like Rényi negativity can detect finite-temperature phase transitions and exhibit universal scaling behavior.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay.
motivation: Understanding the formation of discrete time crystals in open systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics, and the applicability of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism in such systems was unclear.
method: The authors study a dissipative discrete time crystal model and analyze the scaling of spatial defects and transition delay as a function of quench time, using numerical simulations and theoretical scaling arguments.
result: They observe characteristic power-law scaling of defects and transition delay with quench time, consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, indicating universality in the formation process.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism universally governs the formation of discrete time crystals in open systems, providing insights into non-equilibrium phase transitions and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurement devices using only trusted state preparation and measurement, without requiring entanglement or additional resources.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement device to characterize and purify noisy devices through iterative rounds of measurement and correction, leveraging the concept of quantum state verification.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity purified states and measurements, with the required number of rounds scaling polynomially in the desired precision.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and resource-efficient method to mitigate preparation and measurement noise, which is crucial for near-term quantum technologies.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers, achieving sharp spectral features through stabilized lasers and balanced detection.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and resolution in NMR detection of nuclear spin clusters, which is crucial for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use NV centers in diamond to polarize nuclear spins, combined with stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field to resolve NMR signals from multiple spin clusters.
result: They achieve sharp NMR features, enabling the detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters with high sensitivity at room temperature.
conclusion: This work advances the use of NV centers for sensitive NMR detection, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases to transmit information without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing robust information transmission without locally detectable traces.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle for using paraparticles in quantum communication, highlighting their unique advantages.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates gradient scalability in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogate model to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering scalability. Understanding when and why gradients vanish is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the gradient scaling of cost functions in VQAs and introduce a Taylor surrogate model that approximates the cost landscape, enabling efficient gradient estimation.
result: They show that the Taylor surrogate can predict gradient behavior and identify regimes where barren plateaus are avoided, providing a theoretical framework for scalable VQA training.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of trainability in quantum neural networks and offers a practical tool for designing scalable variational algorithms.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing, achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-immune quantum sensor network.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of two ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their generation and readout using cavity-mediated interactions.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states enable Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional spin-squeezed states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments, leveraging hybrid quantum systems (atomic ensembles coupled to cavities).

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic code (likely cat code or binomial code) to protect against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, meaning the error-corrected qubit lives longer than the best unprotected qubit in the same system.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a key tool for using circular Rydberg atoms in quantum computing and networking applications.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum algorithms and information theory, and this work aims to delineate where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of computing matrix functions in different parameter regimes using quantum computational complexity theory, likely employing query complexity or circuit complexity measures.
result: They provide a characterization of the complexity landscape, showing that certain regimes allow for quantum speedups while others remain classically tractable.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into potential quantum advantages for matrix function problems, guiding future algorithm design and complexity classification.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and coherence times under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures and using specific cavity designs can significantly improve stability.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with identified strategies to further reduce decoherence.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling efficient joint model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental data from NV centers.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a scalable and fast approach for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and protocols near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality provides a systematic route to achieve Heisenberg-limited sensing and discusses experimental implementations.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation quantum metrology, with potential applications in fundamental physics and technology.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct better ansätze for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum control examples.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and readily available upgrade for quantum control, enhancing performance without requiring additional hardware resources.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times, demonstrating a practical method for erasure conversion in a superconducting qubit platform.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm is efficient and unifies several symmetry-learning tasks, including learning stabilizer groups and beyond.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithm design and complexity theory.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity enhancement are limited by the number of atoms that can be simultaneously coupled to a single cavity mode; multiplexing addresses this scalability bottleneck.
