method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of phase-separating fluid mixtures with chemical reactions and hydrodynamics.
result: The interplay of reactions, phase separation, and hydrodynamics leads to complex spatiotemporal patterns and chaos.
conclusion: Chemically active emulsions exhibit rich dynamics that can be controlled by reaction rates and fluid properties.

title: Geometric Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse
abstract:
Author(s): Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, and Julien Toulouse

A geometric reformulation of time-dependent density-functional theory better describes nonequilibrium systems.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256401] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A geometric reformulation of time-dependent density functional theory for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: To improve the description of nonequilibrium systems within time-dependent density functional theory.
method: The authors propose a geometric reformulation of the theory.
result: The reformulation better describes nonequilibrium systems.
conclusion: The geometric approach offers a more accurate framework for time-dependent density functional theory in nonequilibrium settings.

title: Emergent Spacetime Supersymmetry At 2d Fractionalized Quantum Criticality
authors: Zhengzhi Wu, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, And Hong Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengzhi Wu, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, and Hong Yao

While experimental evidence for spacetime supersymmetry (SUSY) in particle physics remains elusive, condensed matter systems offer a promising arena for its emergence at quantum critical points (QCPs). Although there have been a variety of proposals for emergent SUSY at symmetry-breaking QCPs, the e…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256502] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes emergent spacetime supersymmetry at a 2D fractionalized quantum critical point in a condensed matter system.
motivation: To find condensed matter realizations of spacetime supersymmetry, which remains elusive in particle physics.
method: The authors study a quantum critical point in a 2D fractionalized system using field-theoretic and numerical methods.
result: They demonstrate that spacetime supersymmetry emerges at the quantum critical point.
conclusion: This provides a new platform for studying supersymmetry in condensed matter systems.

title: Dynamics Of Superconducting Pairs In The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model
authors: G. Sordi, E. M. O’callaghan, C. Walsh, M. Charlebois, P. Sémon, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): G. Sordi, E. M. O’Callaghan, C. Walsh, M. Charlebois, P. Sémon, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

The frequency structure of the superconducting correlations in cuprates gives insights on the pairing mechanism. Here we present an exhaustive study of this problem in the two-dimensional Hubbard model with cellular dynamical mean-field theory. To this end, we systematically quantify the dependence …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256503] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the frequency structure of superconducting correlations in the two-dimensional Hubbard model using cellular dynamical mean-field theory.
motivation: Understanding the pairing mechanism in cuprates is a key open problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) to compute the dynamics of superconducting pairs in the 2D Hubbard model.
result: They systematically quantify the dependence of superconducting correlations on frequency and other parameters.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the pairing mechanism but are primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Edge Reconstruction In A Quantum Spin Hall Insulator
authors: Rahul Soni, Matthias Thamm, Gonzalo Alvarez, Bernd Rosenow, And Adrian Del Maestro
abstract:
Author(s): Rahul Soni, Matthias Thamm, Gonzalo Alvarez, Bernd Rosenow, and Adrian Del Maestro

We study interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a quantum spin Hall insulator described by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Kanamori-Hubbard interactions using the real-space density matrix renormalization group method in both the grand-canonical and canonical ensembles. For a two-dimensional…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256504] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a quantum spin Hall insulator using DMRG, focusing on electronic properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding edge reconstruction in topological insulators is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use real-space density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) in grand-canonical and canonical ensembles to analyze the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Kanamori-Hubbard interactions.
result: They observe interaction-driven edge reconstruction in a two-dimensional quantum spin Hall insulator.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of topological insulators but does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Hearing The Light: Stray-Field Noise From The Emergent Photon In Quantum Spin Ice
authors: Gautam K. Naik, Jonathan N. Hallén, Nishan C. Jayarama, Roderich Moessner, And Chris R. Laumann
abstract:
Author(s): Gautam K. Naik, Jonathan N. Hallén, Nishan C. Jayarama, Roderich Moessner, and Chris R. Laumann

Decisive experimental confirmation of the U(1) quantum spin liquid phase in quantum spin ice remains an outstanding challenge. In this Letter, we propose stray-field magnetometry as a direct probe of the emergent photons—the gapless excitation of the emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice. The…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256705] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes stray-field magnetometry to detect emergent photons in quantum spin ice, a condensed matter system.
motivation: Experimental confirmation of U(1) quantum spin liquid remains challenging; the paper aims to provide a direct probe of emergent photons.
method: The authors theoretically analyze stray-field noise from emergent electrodynamics in quantum spin ice and propose magnetometry as a detection method.
result: They show that stray-field noise spectra exhibit signatures of the emergent photon, enabling experimental verification.
conclusion: Stray-field magnetometry is a viable technique to detect emergent photons in quantum spin ice, advancing the search for quantum spin liquids.

title: Block-Type Antiferromagnetism In Single Chain Quasi-One-Dimensional ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$
authors: Fei Gao, Nikhil Dhale, Ling-Fang Lin, Keith M. Taddei, Yang Zhang, Clarina Dela Cruz, Elbio Dagotto, And Bing Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Fei Gao, Nikhil Dhale, Ling-Fang Lin, Keith M. Taddei, Yang Zhang, Clarina Dela Cruz, Elbio Dagotto, and Bing Lv

One-dimensional (1D) structures provide a unique platform to study the correlated quantum interactions and phase transitions such as unconventional magnetism and superconducting states. Here, we report that iron chalcogenide [MATH] exhibits an unusual bl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256706] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports an unusual block-type antiferromagnetic order in a quasi-one-dimensional iron chalcogenide, studied via neutron scattering and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of quasi-1D iron chalcogenides, which may host unconventional magnetism and superconductivity.
method: Single-crystal neutron diffraction and density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to determine the magnetic structure and exchange interactions.
result: A block-type antiferromagnetic order with ferromagnetically coupled Fe dimers arranged antiferromagnetically along the chain was observed.
conclusion: The findings reveal a novel magnetic ground state in 1D iron chalcogenides, highlighting the rich physics of low-dimensional quantum magnets.

title: Close Proximity To A Quantum Phase Transition In ${\mathrm{TmZn}}_{2}{\mathrm{GaO}}_{5}$
authors: Matthew Ennis, Rabindranath Bag, Tessa Cookmeyer, Matthew B. Stone, Alexander I. Kolesnikov, Tao Hong, Leon Balents, And Sara Haravifard
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Ennis, Rabindranath Bag, Tessa Cookmeyer, Matthew B. Stone, Alexander I. Kolesnikov, Tao Hong, Leon Balents, and Sara Haravifard

[MATH] is a newly synthesized triangular lattice magnet that exhibits a unique quantum phase characterized by strong Ising anisotropy, a pseudodoublet crystal electric field ground state, and a low-energy gapped excitation at the [MATH] point. Unlike its well-known coun…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256707] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of a triangular lattice magnet TmZn2GaO5, which exhibits a quantum phase with strong Ising anisotropy and a gapped excitation, and is close to a quantum phase transition.
motivation: To discover and understand new quantum materials that host exotic magnetic phases, particularly those near quantum critical points.
method: Neutron scattering and thermodynamic measurements on single crystals of TmZn2GaO5, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: The material shows a unique quantum phase with a pseudodoublet ground state and a low-energy gapped excitation at the M point, distinct from its parent compound.
conclusion: TmZn2GaO5 is a promising platform for studying quantum phase transitions and frustrated magnetism in triangular lattices.

title: Critical Phenomenon Inside Asymptotically Flat Black Holes With Spontaneous Scalarization
authors: Li Li, Ze Sun, And Fu-Guo Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Li Li, Ze Sun, and Fu-Guo Yang

We study the nonlinear interior dynamics of spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with zero cosmological constant, revealing novel critical phenomena. We demonstrate that, for a wide range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings, scalarized black holes possess no smooth …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251402] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies critical phenomena inside spontaneously scalarized black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory.
motivation: To understand the nonlinear interior dynamics and critical behavior of scalarized black holes with zero cosmological constant.
method: Numerical simulations and analysis of the Einstein-Maxwell-scalar field equations.
result: Discovery of novel critical phenomena for a wide range of scalar-electromagnetic couplings, showing that scalarized black holes have no smooth interior.
conclusion: The interior dynamics of scalarized black holes exhibit critical behavior that differs from standard black hole interiors.

title: Black Hole Thermodynamics Without Black Hole Solutions
authors: Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, And H. Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, and H. Lü

We consider the string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and show that we can derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes without having to construct the black hole solutions. We argue that the technique can be applied more broadly to string theor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251403] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives black hole thermodynamic quantities from a string-inspired theory without explicitly constructing black hole solutions.
motivation: To show that black hole thermodynamics can be obtained from the theory's structure alone, bypassing the need for explicit solutions.
method: Using the Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and symmetry arguments to extract thermodynamic quantities.
result: Complete set of thermodynamic quantities for charged black holes derived without solving the field equations.
conclusion: The technique is broadly applicable to string theory and may simplify the study of black hole thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Damping Of Cosmological Shear: A New Prediction From Loop Quantum Cosmologies
authors: Wen-Cong Gan, Leila L. Graef, Rudnei O. Ramos, Gustavo S. Vicente, And Anzhong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Cong Gan, Leila L. Graef, Rudnei O. Ramos, Gustavo S. Vicente, and Anzhong Wang

We study the dynamics of the Bianchi I universe in modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) and uncover a robust mechanism for isotropization: the shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independently of the equation of state of standard …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of Bianchi I universe in modified loop quantum cosmology and finds a robust isotropization mechanism via shear damping after the bounce.
motivation: To understand the isotropization process in the early universe within the framework of loop quantum cosmology, which is a quantum gravity theory.
method: The authors analyze the Bianchi I model in modified loop quantum cosmology (mLQC-I) and derive the evolution equations for the shear scalar, solving them numerically for various equations of state.
result: They find that shear is dynamically suppressed after the bounce and decays rapidly in the quantum postbounce regime, independent of the equation of state.
conclusion: This provides a new prediction from loop quantum cosmology that could be tested against cosmological observations.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain
authors: Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, and Y. P. Wang

Non-Hermitian systems have attracted considerable research interest due to their capacity to host unconventional physical phenomena. However, research on pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in one-dimensional non-Hermitian settings remain relatively limited. Here, we propose a one-…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063736] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unconventional phenomena, but pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in 1D are underexplored.
method: The authors propose a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain model and analyze its spectral and localization properties.
result: They observe pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization transitions.
conclusion: The work reveals new aspects of non-Hermitian physics but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Fermionic non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories In $(2+1)$ Dimensions With Built-in Gauge Protection
authors: Gaia de Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Gaia De Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, and Fabian Grusdt

Recent advancements in the field of quantum simulation have significantly expanded the potential for applications, particularly in the context of lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Maintaining gauge invariance throughout a simulation remains a central challenge, especially for large-scale non-Abelian LG…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063327] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum simulation scheme for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories in (2+1) dimensions with built-in gauge protection.
motivation: Simulating non-Abelian lattice gauge theories on quantum devices is challenging due to gauge violations; the authors aim to design a scheme that inherently preserves gauge invariance.
method: They develop a digital quantum simulation protocol using ultracold atoms or trapped ions, incorporating gauge protection via energy penalties and symmetry constraints.
result: The scheme demonstrates robust gauge invariance and scalability for small lattices, with numerical evidence of correct dynamics.
conclusion: The approach offers a viable path to simulating non-Abelian gauge theories on near-term quantum simulators, though experimental realization remains challenging.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci
abstract:
Author(s): Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, and Andrew A. Geraci

Optically levitated dielectric objects are promising for precision force, acceleration, torque, and rotation sensing due to their extreme environmental decoupling. While many levitated optomechanics experiments employ spherical objects, for some applications nonspherical geometries offer advantages.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063529] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework for optimal displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric objects using optical radiation.
motivation: Optically levitated objects are promising for precision sensing, but existing detection methods are optimized for spherical objects; nonspherical geometries offer advantages but lack a general detection theory.
method: The authors develop a general theory for displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped dielectric particles using optical radiation, considering the particle's shape and orientation.
result: They derive optimal detection limits and show that nonspherical particles can achieve higher sensitivity for certain degrees of freedom.
conclusion: The framework enables optimal design of levitated optomechanics experiments with nonspherical particles for enhanced sensing.

title: Geometric Theory Of Constrained Schrödinger Dynamics With Application To Time-dependent Density-functional Theory On A Finite Lattice
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse
abstract:
Author(s): Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, and Julien Toulouse

Time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is a central tool for studying the dynamical electronic structure of molecules and solids, yet aspects of its mathematical foundations remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we revisit the foundations of TDDFT within a finite-dimensional sett…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062222] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric theory of constrained Schrödinger dynamics and applies it to time-dependent density-functional theory on a finite lattice.
motivation: The mathematical foundations of TDDFT are not fully understood, especially for finite-dimensional systems.
method: The authors formulate the dynamics as a constrained Hamiltonian system on a Grassmann manifold and derive the equations of motion using geometric mechanics.
result: They obtain a rigorous derivation of the TDDFT equations for finite lattice systems and prove existence and uniqueness of solutions.
conclusion: The work provides a solid mathematical foundation for TDDFT on finite lattices, but it is primarily a contribution to mathematical physics and density-functional theory, not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Systematic Errors From Inhomogeneous Alkali-spin Polarization In Nmr Gyroscopes And Comagnetometers
authors: Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, And Nan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, and Nan Zhao

Isotope shift, a systematic error arising from the alkali polarization field generated by the spin-exchange collisions between the Xe and alkali-metal atoms, has been observed in many [MATH] comagnetometer studies. This isotope shift constitutes a major source of syste…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062816] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes systematic errors from inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization in NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.
motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major systematic error in comagnetometer studies, and understanding its origin is crucial for improving measurement accuracy.
method: The authors theoretically model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the effect of inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization on the NMR signals.
result: They quantify the isotope shift and show how it depends on experimental parameters such as alkali density and magnetic field gradients.
conclusion: The findings provide a framework to correct for this systematic error, enhancing the precision of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Ultrafast Three-dimensional Steering Of Electronic Ring Currents In Benzene: Coherent Control Of Angular Momentum
authors: Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, And Yonggang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, and Yonggang Yang

Coherent control of electronic ring currents enables the steering of optomagnetic responses on femtosecond timescales. However, most existing schemes confine these currents to the molecular plane, effectively constraining the electronic angular momentum (EAM) vector to a fixed direction. Here, we de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063115] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of electronic ring currents in benzene to steer the electronic angular momentum vector in three dimensions on femtosecond timescales.
motivation: Existing schemes confine ring currents to the molecular plane, limiting the direction of electronic angular momentum. The authors aim to achieve full three-dimensional control.
method: Using tailored laser pulses with specific polarization and timing, they simulate the dynamics of electronic ring currents in benzene via quantum chemical calculations.
result: They show that the electronic angular momentum vector can be steered in three dimensions, enabling ultrafast control of optomagnetic responses.
conclusion: This work opens possibilities for ultrafast optomagnetic devices and coherent control of molecular magnetism.

title: Two-color Laser Cooling With The Rubidium Optical Clock Transition
authors: Wictor C. Magno And Flavio C. Cruz
abstract:
Author(s): Wictor C. Magno and Flavio C. Cruz

The three-level [MATH] cascade transition of [MATH] is widely used as a reference for optical frequency standards based on two-photon spectroscopy, implemented with either single-color excitation at 778 nm or two-color excitation at 780 and 776 n…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063114] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a two-color laser cooling scheme using the rubidium optical clock transition.
motivation: Laser cooling is essential for quantum experiments, but the rubidium clock transition has not been used for cooling before.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-color cooling scheme on the 5S-5P-5D cascade transition in rubidium.
result: They find that two-color cooling can achieve sub-Doppler temperatures and high capture velocities.
conclusion: The proposed scheme could enable new cooling techniques for rubidium atoms, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer
authors: B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, And M. Dupont-Nivet
abstract:
Author(s): B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, and M. Dupont-Nivet

We have realized an interferometer using a thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on a chip. The interferometer resembles a Ramsey interferometer with a state selective spatial splitting of the two internal states as proposed by [M. Ammar et al.,
tldr: This paper demonstrates a Ramsey-type interferometer using a thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on an atom chip.
motivation: Atom-chip interferometers offer compact, scalable platforms for precision measurements, but realizing a Ramsey interferometer with thermal atoms on a chip is challenging due to decoherence and spatial splitting requirements.
method: The authors use a state-selective spatial splitting of two internal states of Rb-87 atoms in a magnetic trap on an atom chip, implementing a Ramsey interferometry sequence.
result: They successfully observe interference fringes, demonstrating the feasibility of a Ramsey interferometer with thermal atoms on a chip.
conclusion: This work advances atom-chip interferometry, potentially enabling compact sensors for inertial forces and fundamental physics tests.

title: Resolution Of The Hyperfine Puzzle And Its Significance For Two-fermion Dirac Atoms
authors: Gordon Baym And Glennys R. Farrar
abstract:
Author(s): Gordon Baym and Glennys R. Farrar

If we could shrink the ground-state wave function of a hydrogen atom to a size [MATH], at fixed electron mass and charge, the singlet hyperfine attraction in a spin singlet state would scale as [MATH]—faster than the increase in kinetic energy—raising the question of why the hyperfine interaction …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062219] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves a puzzle in the hyperfine structure of two-fermion Dirac atoms, focusing on the scaling of hyperfine attraction in hydrogen-like systems.
motivation: The hyperfine interaction in a spin singlet state scales faster than kinetic energy when the wave function is shrunk, raising a fundamental question about stability.
method: The authors analyze the Dirac equation for two-fermion systems and compute the hyperfine splitting, resolving the apparent puzzle through careful relativistic treatment.
result: They show that the hyperfine attraction does not lead to instability, and the puzzle is resolved by considering the full relativistic dynamics.
conclusion: The work clarifies a long-standing issue in atomic physics, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for quantum information science, and the authors aim to extend it to nonlinear and spatially structured regimes.
method: Theoretical analysis of a hexapartite active nonlinear feedback control system based on two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump.
result: The system enables control over multiple nonclassical beams, but the work is primarily a theoretical proposal without experimental demonstration or clear connection to core quantum information tasks.
conclusion: The proposed scheme may be useful for quantum information applications, but its relevance to the specified research directions is limited.

title: Bistable Fourth Sound Resonance In Superfluid $^{3}\mathrm{He}\text{−}\mathrm{B}$ Due To Gap Suppression
authors: Alexander J. Shook, Daksh Malhotra, Aymar Muhikira, And John P. Davis
abstract:

Superfluidity in [MATH] exhibits many unique properties that are of interest to modern condensed matter research, including multiple superfluid phase transitions, topological defects, and exotic classes of excitations like Majorana and Weyl fermions. Many of the most interesting theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214519] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bistable fourth sound resonance in superfluid 3He-B due to gap suppression, a condensed matter phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear acoustic effects in superfluid 3He-B, which exhibits topological defects and exotic excitations.
method: Experimental observation of bistable fourth sound resonance and theoretical modeling of gap suppression.
result: Demonstration of bistability in fourth sound resonance attributed to superfluid gap suppression.
conclusion: The work provides insight into nonlinear dynamics in superfluid 3He-B but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Many-body Wave Function And Edge Magnetization Of An Open $p+is$ Superconducting Chain
authors: Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, And Wang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Jiao, Chao Xu, Congjun Wu, and Wang Yang

Although BCS wave functions for superconductors under periodic boundary conditions are well established, obtaining an explicit form of the many-body BCS wave function under open boundary condition is usually a nontrivial problem. In this work, we construct the exact BCS ground-state wave function of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224525] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs the exact BCS ground-state wave function for an open p+is superconducting chain and studies its edge magnetization.
motivation: BCS wave functions under open boundary conditions are nontrivial but important for understanding edge properties of topological superconductors.
method: The authors derive the exact many-body wave function using a combination of Bogoliubov transformation and solving the BdG equations with open boundaries.
result: They obtain an explicit form of the ground state and compute the edge magnetization, revealing topological edge modes.
conclusion: The work provides a rare exact solution for a superconducting chain with open boundaries, clarifying edge physics in p+is superconductors.

title: Flat-band Driven Kondo Breakdown And Reentrant Effects In Heavy-fermion Moiré Superlattices
authors: Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Eickhoff, Jian-Xin Zhu, and Benedikt Fauseweh

With the recent discovery of van der Waals [MATH]-e…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235153] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo breakdown and reentrant effects in heavy-fermion moiré superlattices, focusing on strongly correlated electronic phenomena.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in van der Waals heterostructures can host emergent electronic phenomena similar to bulk strongly correlated materials, motivating the study of heavy-fermion physics in these systems.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo lattice model in moiré superlattices, exploring flat-band effects on Kondo screening and breakdown.
result: They find that flat bands can drive Kondo breakdown and lead to reentrant heavy-fermion behavior as a function of doping or temperature.
conclusion: The work reveals new aspects of heavy-fermion physics in moiré systems, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Orbital Magnetization Reveals Multiband Topology
authors: Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, And Wojciech J. Jankowski
abstract:
Author(s): Chun Wang Chau, Robert-Jan Slager, and Wojciech J. Jankowski

We demonstrate that nontrivial multiband topological invariants of electronic wave functions can be revealed through orbital magnetization responses to external magnetic fields. We find that decomposing orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions allows one to deduce non…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235154] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that orbital magnetization responses can reveal multiband topological invariants in electronic systems.
motivation: To find a way to probe nontrivial multiband topology through experimentally accessible quantities.
method: Decompose orbital magnetization into energetic and quantum-geometric contributions and relate them to topological invariants.
result: The decomposition allows deduction of multiband topological invariants from magnetization responses.
conclusion: Orbital magnetization is a useful probe for multiband topology, linking quantum geometry to observable responses.

title: Tracking Doublon-holon Dynamics In High-harmonic Generation From Mott Insulators
authors: Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, And Ruifeng Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Tao-Yuan Du, Hui-Ru Li, Bo Li, and Ruifeng Lu

High-harmonic generation (HHG) in strongly correlated Mott insulators is investigated using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain. By projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands, we use the doublon population and its dynamic…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245147] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies high-harmonic generation in Mott insulators using exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of strongly correlated materials, specifically the doublon-holon dynamics underlying HHG in Mott insulators.
method: Exact diagonalization and time-dependent density-matrix propagation of a laser-driven one-dimensional Hubbard chain, projecting onto equilibrium Hubbard bands.
result: The doublon population and its dynamics are tracked, revealing the role of doublon-holon pairs in HHG.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the microscopic mechanism of HHG in strongly correlated systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Strain-driven Antiferroelastic Switching Of Altermagnetism
authors: Fanjunjie Han, Shuaihao Tang, Jian-Dong Sun, Xin-Gang Zhao, And Haiyang Xu
abstract:

Altermagnetism, characterized by pronounced momentum-space spin splitting without net magnetization, provides an emerging platform for spintronics. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 214457] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nonvolatile control of altermagnetic spin states via antiferroelastic lattice distortion.
motivation: Nonvolatile control of spin states in altermagnets is crucial for spintronic device applications.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to show that antiferroelastic distortion can switch the altermagnetic order.
result: They find that strain can induce a reversible switching of the altermagnetic spin splitting.
conclusion: Antiferroelastic switching provides a pathway for electrically controlled altermagnetic spintronics.

title: Spin Transfer Torque Induced Deterministic Néel Vector Switching In Altermagnets
authors: Yuriy G. Semenov And Ki Wook Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yuriy G. Semenov and Ki Wook Kim

The process of spin-transfer torque in an altermagnet (AM) is theoretically investigated from the perspective of disparate effective exchange fields acting on the two sublattices. The momentum dependent, anisotropic spin splitting in the AM band structure can cause this asymmetry, leading ultimately…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224444] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates spin-transfer torque in altermagnets, focusing on Néel vector switching driven by asymmetric exchange fields.
motivation: Altermagnets are a new class of magnetic materials with potential for spintronic applications; understanding spin-transfer torque in these systems is crucial for device development.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on the momentum-dependent anisotropic spin splitting in the altermagnet band structure to compute spin-transfer torque and Néel vector dynamics.
result: They find that the disparate effective exchange fields on the two sublattices can induce deterministic Néel vector switching via spin-transfer torque.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for using altermagnets in spintronic devices, but it is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Loss/gain-induced Hall Effect Of Vortex Light
authors: Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, And Kai Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Yucheng Lai, Yongliang Zhang, and Kai Chang

The Hall effect provides a route for unidirectional manipulations of classical and quantum waves. In optics, the spin Hall effect (SHE) induced by the interaction between intrinsic angular momentum (AM) and material inhomogeneity enables AM-dependent control of light at the subwavelength scale. Desp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245309] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a loss/gain-induced Hall effect for vortex light in photonic systems, focusing on classical wave propagation.
motivation: To explore how non-Hermitian effects (loss/gain) can induce a Hall-like effect for optical vortices, extending the concept of spin Hall effect to orbital angular momentum.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a photonic system with engineered loss and gain, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and calculating the transverse deflection of vortex beams.
result: They demonstrate that loss/gain gradients can produce a Hall effect for vortex light, analogous to the spin Hall effect but driven by orbital angular momentum.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for controlling light propagation using non-Hermitian photonics, with potential applications in optical manipulation and information processing.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, and Matthew E. Potter

Isotopic substitution modifies nuclear masses without altering the electronic potential-energy surface to first order and is therefore often interpreted as a simple rescaling of vibrational frequencies. In solids with dense phonon manifolds, however, mass substitution acts as a parametric Hermitian …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotope substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, focusing on collective mixing effects.
motivation: Isotope substitution is often assumed to simply rescale vibrational frequencies, but in dense phonon manifolds, mass changes can cause significant mode mixing and transport, which is not well understood.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the parametric Hermitian perturbation induced by mass substitution, examining eigenvector transport and collective phonon mixing.
result: They find that isotope substitution leads to nontrivial mixing of phonon modes and transport of eigenvectors across the Brillouin zone, challenging the simple frequency rescaling picture.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of considering collective phonon dynamics in isotope-substituted solids, with implications for thermal transport and material properties.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, And Yu-Jun Zhao

motivation: Existing studies on stacking-induced unconventional magnetism are limited to specific materials and configurations, lacking a general theoretical framework.
method: The authors propose a stacking theory based on symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations to classify and predict magnetic properties of bilayer 2D magnets.
result: The theory successfully explains known phenomena and predicts new magnetic phases in various bilayer systems.
conclusion: The stacking theory provides a systematic approach to engineer magnetism in bilayer 2D materials, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Antiferromagnetic Solitons In NiO As Possible Entities For Logic Operations
authors: Z. Li, T. Chirac, J. Tranchida, J.-Y. Chauleau, And M. Viret

motivation: To explore antiferromagnetic materials as a platform for high-speed logic devices using solitons.
method: Atomistic simulations of NiO stripes to model spin wave and domain wall propagation.
result: Demonstrates fast velocities over 40 km/s and interesting propagation properties enabling crossing of solitons.
conclusion: Antiferromagnetic solitons in NiO show promise for logic operations due to their speed and propagation characteristics.

title: Nontrivial Three-sublattice Magnetization In The Easy-axis Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Xxz Antiferromagnet On The Triangular Lattice
authors: Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, And Satoshi Nishimoto

method: Density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) with spiral boundary conditions to map finite clusters onto 1D chains.
result: Identifies a nontrivial three-sublattice magnetic order in the easy-axis regime.
conclusion: The work contributes to the understanding of frustrated quantum magnetism but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Strongly Quenched Kramers Doublet Magnetism In ${\mathrm{SmMgAl}}_{11}{\mathrm{O}}_{19}$
authors: Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, And Ross H. Colman

We report magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements on the rare-earth hexaaluminate [MATH], where [MATH] realizes a strongly quenched Kramers doublet on a triangular lattice with an exceptionally weak net exchan…

motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of SmMgAl11O19, a rare-earth hexaaluminate with a triangular lattice, and characterize its low-energy magnetic behavior.
method: Magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements were performed on single crystals of SmMgAl11O19.
result: The compound exhibits a strongly quenched Kramers doublet with exceptionally weak net exchange interactions, leading to a low-temperature magnetic state dominated by single-ion physics.
conclusion: The material provides a platform for studying frustrated magnetism in a triangular lattice with minimal exchange coupling, but the work is purely experimental condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spin-dependent Orbital Selectivity And Partial Kondo-like Screening In The Magnetically Ordered Hund's Metal ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoO}}_{4}$
authors: Shivani Bhardwaj And Sudhir K. Pandey
abstract:

motivation: Hund's metals are a rare class of correlated materials where Hund's coupling dominates over Hubbard U, and Sr2CoO4 is a candidate with unusual properties that need theoretical understanding.

result: They find spin-dependent orbital selectivity and partial Kondo-like screening in the magnetically ordered state, with different Co orbitals exhibiting distinct correlation effects.
conclusion: The study reveals complex interplay between magnetism, orbital selectivity, and Kondo physics in Hund's metals, providing insights into their electronic behavior.

title: Quasiparticle Interference In LiFeAs: Signature Of Inelastic Tunneling Through Spin Fluctuations
authors: Shun Chi, Carolina A. Marques, W. N. Hardy, Ruixing Liang, Pinder Dosanjh, D. A. Bonn, S. A. Burke, And Peter Wahl
abstract:

Quasiparticle interference (QPI) is a powerful tool to characterize the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in unconventional superconductors, by mapping the spatial dependence of elastic tunneling of electrons between the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope and a sample. Here, we con…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235148] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle interference in the iron-based superconductor LiFeAs, focusing on inelastic tunneling through spin fluctuations.

result: The observed interference patterns are consistent with inelastic tunneling via spin fluctuations, providing insight into the electronic structure and pairing.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of spin fluctuations in the tunneling process, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Orbital Hybridization Induces Giant Cubic Rashba Effect At The $\text{Cu/}{\mathrm{WO}}_{3}$ Interface
authors: Md Aktar Hossain And Saikat Das
abstract:

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:

motivation: To understand the impact of dissipation on nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals using a 1D model.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model and derive the energy spectrum to identify exceptional rings.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D system, analogous to Weyl exceptional lines in 3D.

motivation: To classify and construct exactly solvable many-body models with Jastrow wave functions on arbitrary graphs.
method: The authors define interactions via the adjacency matrix of a graph and derive parent Hamiltonians for which the Jastrow wave function is the ground state.
result: A taxonomy of integrable and ground-state solvable models is established, linking graph theory to many-body physics.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic framework for constructing solvable models, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: They find that the resistivity shows a distinct temperature dependence and anisotropy arising from the toroidal Fermi surface.
conclusion: The geometry of the Fermi surface significantly influences phonon-limited transport in nodal-line semimetals, providing insights into their electronic properties.

tldr: This paper studies decoherence of free electrons due to electromagnetic interactions, with applications in electron microscopy.
motivation: Understanding decoherence in electron beams is crucial for improving spatial coherence in electron microscopy, which relies on interference and diffraction for atomic-scale imaging.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to model decoherence arising from inelastic scattering processes, likely using quantum electrodynamics or a semiclassical approach.
result: They quantify the decoherence effect and its impact on electron beam coherence, providing insights into the limits of electron microscopy resolution.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of free-electron decoherence, offering a foundation for mitigating decoherence in electron microscopy and related techniques.

motivation: Understanding the emergence of multiple zero modes in extended topological Josephson junctions is important for topological quantum computing, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Controlled Pairing Symmetries In A Fermi-Hubbard Ladder With Band Flattening
authors: João P. Mendonça, S. Biswas, M. Dziurawiec, U. Bhattacharya, K. Jachymski, M. Aidelsburger, M. Lewenstein, M. M. Maśka, And T. Grass

The competition between interactions in systems with slow electrons can drive unusual collective behavior. These findings offer a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.

method: The authors analyze a microscopic ladder model with diagonal hopping and complex loop-like exchange interactions, using theoretical and numerical methods to study the competition between pairing mechanisms.
result: Both mechanisms independently suppress metallic behavior but stabilize completely different spatial patterns of electron pairing.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning the competition between pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.

conclusion: FeRh is a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.

method: The author develops a lattice gas model that captures the coupling between electronic, ionic, and mass degrees of freedom, and analyzes phase transitions using mean-field theory and Monte Carlo simulations.

method: Numerical simulations of two kinetic wealth-exchange models (Banerjee and yard-sale) and two earthquake models (two-fractal overlap and Olami-Feder-Christensen), computing Gini, Kolkata, and other inequality indices.
result: Inequality measures show similar patterns across models, with the Kolkata index exhibiting a universal value near 0.8 at criticality.
conclusion: Inequality measures may serve as universal indicators of criticality in complex systems, but the work is purely classical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Effect Of Temporary Lockdowns On Disease Extinction Risk In Assortative Networks
authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf

method: The authors use a stochastic susceptible-infected-recovered (SIR) model on assortative networks and derive analytical expressions for the extinction probability using branching process approximations and generating functions.
result: They find that temporary lockdowns can significantly increase the extinction probability, and the effect depends on the timing and duration of the lockdown as well as the network assortativity.
conclusion: Temporary lockdowns can be an effective strategy to increase disease extinction risk, but their success is sensitive to network structure and intervention timing.

title: Theory Uncertainties In Predictions Of Strong-field Qed

title: Stochastic Acceleration Of Electrons In Fluctuating Fields Induced By Stimulated Raman Scattering In Subrelativistic Laser-plasma Interactions

conclusion: Stochastic acceleration is a key mechanism for electron energization in subrelativistic laser-plasma interactions, with implications for fusion and astrophysics.

conclusion: The framework provides a powerful tool for modeling and controlling pattern dynamics in complex geometries.

method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe rare cage escape events.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism for structural relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems and challenge existing theories of relaxation.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; bridging this gap is necessary to validate quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new computational complexity arguments, likely involving approximate average-case hardness and anticoncentration, adapted to the saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with modes.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible conjectures, extending the theoretical basis for quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for current photonic quantum advantage experiments, confirming that they are indeed hard to simulate classically.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and can be detected via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum behavior of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential implications for condensed matter physics.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed to describe chiral solitons, and their low-energy properties are analyzed using bosonization and Luttinger liquid theory.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral solitons and suggests experimental signatures, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions and uncovers emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of strongly coupled conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a novel numerical approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the theory while preserving rotational symmetry, and perform numerical simulations.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the low-energy spectrum of the free and interacting fermionic theories.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying fermionic CFTs and can reveal emergent symmetries not manifest in the UV description.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré superstructures is important for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based information manipulation.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures for potential applications in information technology.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures is crucial for designing spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the behavior of topological magnon gaps near the Curie point.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie temperature.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting inherent hardness.
conclusion: Simple neural networks may be suitable for cryptographic applications requiring collision resistance.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks without requiring detailed knowledge of the dynamics.
method: The authors propose a framework that leverages physical principles to infer causal relationships from observed network dynamics.
result: The framework is demonstrated to accurately predict links across a variety of networked systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a versatile tool for understanding causal structures in complex networks.

abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers via topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or topological methods.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.

authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transition of the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which may exhibit novel magnetic behavior.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the magnetic phase transition.
result: The system undergoes a three-dimensional XY universality class transition, and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking is observed in the ground state.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic properties of kagome spin ice materials, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most known flat bands require cryogenic temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, with tunability via material composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for investigating strongly correlated electron physics at accessible temperatures, potentially enabling new quantum devices.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material with potential for topological phases.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy combined with magneto-optical measurements under varying electric fields.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field-driven transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a platform for studying and controlling quantum anomalous Hall states, with implications for topological electronics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective explores how biomolecular condensation in living cells can process high-dimensional information through phase transitions.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, and biomolecular condensates may offer a powerful computational framework.
method: The authors discuss theoretical concepts of phase separation and condensation as information-processing mechanisms, drawing analogies to physical computation.
result: They propose that condensates can classify and respond to signals by exploiting phase transitions, enabling high-dimensional sensing.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a novel paradigm for cellular computation, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not established.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations, at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to investigate the critical properties of a model of spinning particles that form hyperuniform fluids.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The findings reveal new critical phenomena in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to soft matter physics.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies unexpected residual scattering in stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments reveal residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals are performed, and the scattering is attributed to radiative loss mechanisms.
result: Residual scattering is observed and linked to radiative loss, contradicting the expected transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
result: Observation of spin-dependent electron optics enabling a ballistic spin valve.

result: They identify a dipolar nematic ordering that underpins relaxor ferroelectric properties.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models, challenging the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: To understand how domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries.
result: Demonstrates that the shape of the domain can fundamentally change the ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced phase separation.

result: Discovery of a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium.

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.

tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to constrain topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.

authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin

tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
