Thermal transport in amorphous materials involves a complex interplay between anharmonicity and atomic-scale dynamics, particularly across the glass transition. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, we investigate the temperature dependence of thermal transport in amorphous ${}_{2}{\mat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224318] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal transport in amorphous and supercooled liquid alumina, focusing on vibrational and diffusional contributions.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in amorphous materials is important for applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations and theoretical modeling are used to analyze temperature-dependent thermal conductivity.
result: The study reveals the interplay between vibrational and diffusional heat transport across the glass transition.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into thermal transport mechanisms in amorphous materials but are not relevant to the specified research interests.

title: Odd-parity Altermagnetism: A Spin Group Study
authors: Minghuan Zeng, Zheng Qin, Ling Qin, Shiping Feng, Lin Wu, Dong-Hui Xu, And Rui Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Minghuan Zeng, Zheng Qin, Ling Qin, Shiping Feng, Lin Wu, Dong-Hui Xu, and Rui Wang

Conventional altermagnetism, characterized by the even-parity spin splitting, has been intensively studied. Here, on the basis of spin-group analyses, the authors elucidate necessary conditions for the emergence of odd-parity altermagnetism. It is derived that the odd-parity altermagnetism arises from the following criteria: (i) the breaking nonmagnetic time reversal symmetry; (ii) the collinear compensated magnetism; (iii) the symmetry [C2||E¯] connecting opposite-spin sublattices, where ¯ respectively represent a 180° rotation around the axis perpendicular to spins and the inversion separating opposite-spin sublattices.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220412] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies odd-parity altermagnetism using spin group theory, identifying symmetry conditions for its emergence.
motivation: Altermagnetism is a recently discovered magnetic phase with potential spintronic applications; odd-parity variants have not been systematically studied.
method: The authors perform spin group symmetry analysis to derive necessary conditions for odd-parity altermagnetism, focusing on collinear compensated magnetism and specific symmetries.
result: They find that odd-parity altermagnetism requires breaking nonmagnetic time reversal symmetry, collinear compensated magnetism, and a specific symmetry connecting opposite-spin sublattices.
conclusion: The work establishes a theoretical framework for odd-parity altermagnetism, which may guide future materials discovery.

title: Geomimicry: Emergent Dynamics In Earth-mediated Complex Materials
authors: Shravan Pradeep, Emanuela Del Gado, Douglas J. Jerolmack, And Paulo E. Arratia
abstract:
Author(s): Shravan Pradeep, Emanuela Del Gado, Douglas J. Jerolmack, and Paulo E. Arratia

Soils and sediments are soft, amorphous materials with complex microstructures and mechanical properties. They are also building blocks for industrial materials such as concrete. These Earth-mediated materials evolve under prolonged environmental pressures such as mechanical stress, chemical gradien…



[Phys. Rev. E 113, 061002] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the emergent dynamics of earth-mediated complex materials like soils and sediments under environmental pressures.
motivation: Understanding how soft, amorphous materials evolve under prolonged mechanical and chemical stress is important for geophysics and industrial applications.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical approaches to characterize microstructural and mechanical changes in these materials.
result: The paper reveals emergent behaviors in earth-mediated materials under environmental forcing.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the dynamics of complex natural and industrial materials.

title: Atomic-scale Insights Into Melting And Supercooling Mechanism Of Sodium Acetate Trihydrate Via Molecular Dynamics
authors: Ping Li, Chuanshuai Dong, And Lizhi Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ping Li, Chuanshuai Dong, and Lizhi Zhang

Sodium acetate trihydrate (SAT) is a promising phase change material for thermal energy storage through phase transition, yet its microscopic mechanisms of phase transition, especially melting and intrinsic supercooling, remain unclear. In this study, all-atom molecular-dynamics simulations were per…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065419] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics study of melting and supercooling in sodium acetate trihydrate for thermal energy storage.
motivation: To understand microscopic mechanisms of phase transition in a phase change material for thermal energy storage.
method: All-atom molecular dynamics simulations of sodium acetate trihydrate.
result: Provides atomic-scale insights into melting and supercooling mechanisms.
conclusion: The study clarifies phase transition mechanisms but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: ChronoCast: A Time-series Paradigm For Molecular Dynamics Simulation Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
authors: Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, And Jie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, and Jie Chen

We propose a time-series paradigm named ChronoCast for molecular dynamics simulation using an advanced autoregressive Equivariant Graph Neural Network, which reformulates the conventionally time-consuming integration process into a forecasting task. This reformulation in turn offers a promising solu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065305] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a time-series paradigm using equivariant graph neural networks to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to numerical integration; the authors aim to reformulate integration as a forecasting task to speed up simulations.
method: They develop an autoregressive equivariant graph neural network that predicts future atomic positions and velocities from past trajectory data, treating the simulation as a time-series forecasting problem.
result: The method achieves competitive accuracy with traditional integrators while significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: ChronoCast offers a promising machine learning approach to accelerate molecular dynamics, though it is primarily a computational chemistry/materials science contribution.

title: Redirecting Countermoving Swarms Through Collision
authors: Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy Mcguire, And Ira B. Schwartz
abstract:
Author(s): Jason Hindes, Chinthan B. Prasad, Loy McGuire, and Ira B. Schwartz

Multiswarm systems, where two or more swarms of mobile agents occupy the same region of space with different parameters and goals, occur in a variety of biological, engineering, and defense applications. Composites of multiple swarms can produce hybrid spatiotemporal patterns, which compared to sing…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023351] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of two countermoving swarms that interact through collisions, producing hybrid spatiotemporal patterns.
motivation: Understanding how multiple swarms with different parameters and goals interact is important for biological, engineering, and defense applications.
method: The authors model two swarms of mobile agents moving in opposite directions and analyze their collision dynamics using theoretical and computational approaches.
result: They find that collisions can redirect the swarms, leading to emergent patterns such as mixing, separation, or synchronized motion.
conclusion: Collision-mediated interactions can be exploited to control and redirect multiswarm systems.

title: Estimating Orbital Parameters Of Direct Imaging Exoplanet Using Neural Networks
authors: Bo Liang, Chang Liu, Hanlin Song, Tianyu Zhao, Yuxiang Xu, Zihao Xiao, Manjia Liang, Minghui Du, Wei-Liang Qian, Li-E Qiang, Mingming Sun, Peng Xu, And Ziren Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Liang, Chang Liu, Hanlin Song, Tianyu Zhao, Yuxiang Xu, Zihao Xiao, Manjia Liang, Minghui Du, Wei-Liang Qian, Li-e Qiang, Mingming Sun, Peng Xu, and Ziren Luo

We propose a flow-matching Markov chain Monte Carlo (FM-MCMC) algorithm for estimating the orbital parameters of exoplanetary systems, especially for those in which only one exoplanet is involved. Compared to traditional methods that rely on random sampling within the Bayesian framework, our approac…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023341] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a flow-matching Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for estimating orbital parameters of directly imaged exoplanets.
motivation: Traditional Bayesian methods for exoplanet orbital parameter estimation rely on random sampling and can be inefficient. The authors aim to improve efficiency using a flow-matching approach.
method: The FM-MCMC algorithm combines normalizing flows with Markov chain Monte Carlo to sample from the posterior distribution of orbital parameters.
result: The algorithm demonstrates improved sampling efficiency and accuracy compared to traditional MCMC methods on synthetic and real data.
conclusion: Flow-matching MCMC is a promising tool for exoplanet orbital parameter estimation, offering faster convergence and better exploration of parameter space.

title: Why ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GaTe}}_{2}$ Has Higher Curie Temperature Than ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: Bomin Kim, Tumentsereg Ochirkhuyag, Dorj Odkhuu, And S. H. Rhim
abstract:
Author(s): Bomin Kim, Tumentsereg Ochirkhuyag, Dorj Odkhuu, and S. H. Rhim

Physics of [MATH] having higher Curie temperature [MATH] than [MATH] is explored theoretically in the framework of magnetic exchange interactions. [MATH] and [MATH] ar…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023333] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the origin of higher Curie temperature in Fe3GaTe2 compared to Fe3GeTe2 using magnetic exchange interaction analysis.
motivation: Understanding why Fe3GaTe2 has a higher Curie temperature than Fe3GeTe2 is important for designing two-dimensional magnetic materials with enhanced thermal stability.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations to evaluate magnetic exchange parameters and use Monte Carlo simulations to estimate Curie temperatures.
result: They find that stronger in-plane ferromagnetic exchange interactions in Fe3GaTe2 lead to its higher Curie temperature.
conclusion: The study provides insights into tuning Curie temperatures in van der Waals magnets by chemical substitution.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and evaluate the effects of heat treatment.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and annealing processes to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and the formation of complex domain walls.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were applied to Ni₂MnTeO₆ to probe its ferro-rotational, polar, and chiral domains.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined ferroic properties, which may have implications for multifunctional materials.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and material properties.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper is a review summarizing experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: It highlights the challenges and advances in understanding the electronic and structural properties of these radioactive materials.
conclusion: The review expands our understanding of transplutonium materials but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the multimessenger astrophysics enabled by future detectors.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will advance our understanding of neutron star physics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties constrain the behavior of matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements provide constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search channels, and project discovery potential for the High-Luminosity LHC based on current constraints.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC, but does not present new theoretical or experimental results.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain regions of parameter space, and the HL-LHC will have significant discovery potential across multiple channels.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is the Nobel lecture on Boltzmann machines, a foundational concept in machine learning, not directly related to quantum information theory.
motivation: The lecture presents the development and significance of Boltzmann machines in artificial intelligence.
method: The author describes the architecture and learning algorithm of Boltzmann machines, including hidden units and contrastive divergence.
result: Boltzmann machines can learn complex probability distributions and have been influential in deep learning.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines represent a key contribution to machine learning, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating all data up to the end of 2022.
result: A self-consistent set of values and uncertainties for the fundamental constants is provided, along with detailed documentation of the input data and methodology.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values represent the most accurate and reliable set of fundamental constants, superseding previous adjustments.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: The paper summarizes the state of the art in optoacoustic microscopy and its applications.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for deep-tissue imaging with optical contrast, and ongoing developments enhance its capabilities.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses gravitational wave signals from early universe phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves can probe the first second of the universe, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical predictions for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, along with detection strategies.
result: It summarizes possible signals and detection methods for early universe gravitational waves.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the earliest moments of the universe, complementing other probes.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, describing how Wannier functions are used to transform Bloch states into localized orbitals.
result: The ecosystem enables accurate integrations, topological invariant calculations, and materials design.
conclusion: Wannier functions are a powerful tool in condensed-matter physics, and the software ecosystem supports a wide range of applications.

title: Transient Large-Scale Anisotropy In TeV Cosmic Rays Due To An Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejection
authors: Zhen Cao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Cao et al. (LHAASO Collaboration)

A solar storm hitting Earth appears to have reduced the amount of incoming high-energy cosmic rays, suggesting a new way of measuring solar activity.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251002] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a transient large-scale anisotropy in TeV cosmic rays caused by an interplanetary coronal mass ejection, observed by the LHAASO collaboration.
motivation: To understand how solar storms affect high-energy cosmic rays and to explore a new method for measuring solar activity.
method: Analysis of data from the LHAASO observatory during a solar storm event, measuring the anisotropy of TeV cosmic rays.
result: A significant reduction in incoming high-energy cosmic rays was observed, correlated with the coronal mass ejection.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that solar storms can modulate cosmic ray anisotropy, offering a new probe of solar activity.

title: Search For Dark Matter Induced Airglow In Planetary Atmospheres
authors: Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, And Joshua Tong
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Blanco, Rebecca K. Leane, Marianne Moore, and Joshua Tong

We point out that dark matter (DM) can illuminate planetary skies via ultraviolet airglow. Dark matter annihilation products can excite molecular hydrogen, which then deexcites to produce ultraviolet emission in the Lyman and Werner bands. We search for this new effect by analyzing nightside ultravi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251001] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes that dark matter annihilation in planetary atmospheres can produce ultraviolet airglow, and searches for this signal in nightside ultraviolet observations.
motivation: Dark matter detection is a major goal in physics, and this work explores a new indirect detection channel using planetary atmospheres as targets.
method: The authors model the excitation of molecular hydrogen by dark matter annihilation products and predict ultraviolet emission in Lyman and Werner bands, then analyze existing nightside ultraviolet data from planetary missions.
result: No significant signal is found, and constraints are placed on dark matter annihilation cross-sections.
conclusion: Planetary atmospheres can serve as novel detectors for dark matter, but current data do not show evidence of dark matter-induced airglow.

title: Short Strings In Three-Dimensional Anti–de Sitter Space: From Weak To Strong Coupling
authors: Simon Ekhammar, Nikolay Gromov, Bogdan Stefański, Jr., And Charles Thull
abstract:

tldr: This paper solves the quantum spectral curve for strings in AdS3 with Ramond-Ramond charge, studying the spectrum from weak to strong coupling.
motivation: To understand the spectrum of short strings in three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which is a problem in string theory and holography.
method: Numerical solution of the conjectured quantum spectral curve for the integrable system.
result: At strong coupling, the spectrum organizes into flat-space string mass levels with universal square-root scaling.
conclusion: The work provides a non-perturbative check of the AdS/CFT correspondence and the quantum spectral curve approach.

It is widely assumed that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces a species’ capacity to adapt. However, this hypothesis lacks support at the scale of global change, in part because the distribution of adaptation rates is unknown. Here, we test this idea by formulating a general model t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 254201] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the relationship between global environmental change rates and species extinction, focusing on evolutionary adaptation rates.
motivation: To test the hypothesis that extinction occurs when environmental change outpaces adaptation, at a global scale.
method: Formulates a general model relating rates of global change, evolutionary adaptation, and extinction.
result: Provides a theoretical framework linking these rates, though specific results are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The model supports the idea that extinction risk increases when adaptation cannot keep pace with environmental change.

title: How The Oblique Drift Instability Alters Solar Wind Heating And Constrains The Distribution Of Solar Wind Observations
authors: Mihailo M. Martinović, Kristopher G. Klein, Leon Ofman, Yogesh, Gregory G. Howes, Jaye L. Verniero, Peter H. Yoon, Daniel Verscharen, And Benjamin L. Alterman
abstract:

Excursions beyond these thresholds result in the emission of energy, transferred from particles to coherent elec…

authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti
abstract:

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. motivation: To develop a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators.
method: Combining particle trapping in stable resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber.
result: Successful demonstration of beam extraction over millions of turns using the proposed technique.
conclusion: The technique is a promising option for low-loss slow extraction in high-energy accelerators.

title: Plasma Flow Generation And Particle Acceleration From Expanding Magnetic Bubbles

result: A rising current expels plasma and accelerates particles via expanding magnetic bubbles.
conclusion: The results provide quantitative insights into plasma dynamics in such systems.

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.

tldr: This paper introduces a concept called super-resonance that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonant modes have a limited bandwidth, which restricts their application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The paper theoretically and numerically demonstrates a super-resonance phenomenon that maintains a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance enables broadband flow stabilization and other applications by breaking the traditional bandwidth limit of resonant modes.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new mechanism for achieving broadband resonant behavior, with potential applications in flow control and other fields.

tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and connect these observations to bulk hydrogel behavior.
result: They develop a force-response model that explains fatigue behavior and provides design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work offers insights into molecular-level fatigue mechanisms and practical guidelines for creating more durable soft materials.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights can help improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into QCD, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments, highlighting recent advances from BESIII.
result: BESIII has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems with high-precision data.
conclusion: The review summarizes current knowledge and recent advances in hadron production from open-charm meson pairs, contributing to hadron spectroscopy.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its contributions to various scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial that presents three colloquia highlighting the observatory's achievements.
result: The editorial does not present new research results but commemorates the observatory's scientific impact.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has had a revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes the basics of planetary radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: Arecibo's radar system was the most sensitive of its kind for over two decades, enabling detailed characterization of many Solar System objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss is a major setback for the field.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the history and scientific legacy of the Arecibo 305-m radio telescope, covering its contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
motivation: To provide a historical perspective on Arecibo's impact on radio astronomy and atmospheric science, emphasizing how upgrades expanded its capabilities.
method: The paper is a review, summarizing key scientific achievements across multiple decades and highlighting the telescope's role in various subfields.
result: Arecibo made influential contributions to pulsar timing, neutral hydrogen mapping, interstellar medium characterization, VLBI imaging, SETI, and the detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.
conclusion: Arecibo's legacy endures through its transformative scientific output, despite its collapse in 2020.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's incoherent scatter radar and supporting instruments.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities enabled studies of ionospheric and upper atmospheric physics; this colloquium summarizes key findings.
method: The paper is a review, synthesizing results from radar, lidar, optical, and satellite measurements of the ionosphere and magnetosphere.
result: It highlights advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal layers in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace research, and its closure leaves a gap in observational capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm rain formation is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The authors review the physics of convection-cloud chambers, including turbulent fluctuations and supersaturation, and synthesize experimental, theoretical, and computational results.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can reproduce key cloud processes under controlled conditions, offering insights into the precipitation bottleneck.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising platform for bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales to understand warm rain formation.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae, focusing on detection and parameter estimation.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, and gravitational waves provide unique insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The authors summarize recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discuss detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The paper presents the latest modeling results and signal predictions, but does not introduce new results or methods.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from core collapse supernovae is a promising avenue for multimessenger astronomy, but the paper is a review without novel contributions to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle, using radio galaxy and quasar catalogs.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the large-scale matter distribution with the cosmic microwave background dipole.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to assess the compatibility of the matter dipole with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency between the two dipoles is found, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require new physics beyond ΛCDM.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of astrophysical tests of self-interacting dark matter, focusing on dark sector interactions and halo dynamics.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter by testing self-interaction models using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of theoretical models and observational constraints from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.
